output.brief:
Don't discipline drivers or run retraining. The evidence points to contaminated brake fluid. Eleven vans were serviced at Northfield Motor Services using fluid from one old bulk drum with a missing cap. All 11 vans with complaints are among those. Two other vans, serviced from a fresh drum, have no complaints. Two vans returned on 24 Sep tested at 149–152°C boiling point, against 255°C for sealed stock. That is water-contaminated fluid, which can vaporise on long descents and make the pedal go soft. The same drivers report no brake problems in other vans on the same hills. Pad batches were spread across both outside garages, and Upper Wend exposure was similar for all vans. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep, but nobody replied.

Do now: take all 13 Northfield-serviced vans off the road, or at least the 11 from the old drum. Test their fluid, renew it from sealed stock, and return them to the pool. Check whether Calder Road's fluid source was sound. Drop the disciplinary plan, since reporting protected safety. Don't rush a pad supplier switch. Confidence is high, but the remaining uncertainty is whether Calder's fluid is fine. Eight of the 11 vans were not retested.
